name: Ui_Screen_Ctor_vt7609AC
summary: Constructor of one UI/field screen class: runs the shared Ui_Screen_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x7609AC, resets the embedded member slot and clears the three 'no id / no selection' words at +0x125C..+0x1264.
evidence: The caller is now the named Field_ObjectFactory_Kind47 and the base is Ui_Screen_CtorBase (0.70), so 'constructor of a screen-family object' is certain; nothing identifies which screen, so the vtable stays in the name.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_PlayDamageAnim
summary: Resolves the element's actor by handle, skips if its state-2 query is non-zero, asks for the default motion id, verifies the actor can play it (vtable +0x84) and starts it with a battle-RNG delay.
evidence: New named callees Menu_FindActorByHandle and Actor_GetDefaultMotionId plus the battle RNG at work+0x4218 confirm 'play the default motion with jitter'; there is still no caller or vtable slot that proves this is the damage reaction, so the maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_PlayStatePoseIfSet
summary: Minimal pose replay: resolves the unit's actor by handle, asks Battle_SelectPoseGroup which pose group applies and plays it through 0x005E7848 only when the group is non-zero.
evidence: Same named callee triple as 0x002DAF74 (Menu_FindActorByHandle, Battle_SelectPoseGroup, 0x005E7848) and no 0x669DD4 ready check; which unit state reaches this variant is still unknown.

name: maybe_Battle_Actor_UpdateIdleState
summary: Battle actor-action timer: once the value returned by 0x00669D38 exceeds ~1.0 it resolves the actor by handle and replays its selected pose group, returning the actor to a stance after a second without action.
evidence: The pose helpers are named (Menu_FindActorByHandle, Battle_SelectPoseGroup) but the compared value arrives in an unrecovered float register (in_s0) and 0x00669D38 is unnamed, so the timer/'idle' reading is only an interpretation.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_PlayStatePoseWhenFlagged
summary: Element-side pose replay: when the element flag at +0x2C is set or the actor passes the 0x00669DD4 ready check, resolves the actor by handle and plays the pose group selected by Battle_SelectPoseGroup.
evidence: The named callee triple (Menu_FindActorByHandle, Battle_SelectPoseGroup, 0x005E7848) plus the +0x2C flag test is clear, but the element class is still inferred only from the 0x3FBxxx neighbourhood and there are no direct callers.

name: maybe_Ui_JockeyPanel_OnDecide
summary: Commits the panel's current grid cell in UI mode 0xD: packs the two cursor indices and the cell kind, writes the value into the grid table at work+0x24A98+0x57D4 (+0x15F3 byte plane), fires command 0xAE, notifies the scene flow and closes the panel.
evidence: The flow is now supported by named Ui_Slot_GetState/Ui_Slot_GetScale and maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_OnOpen, but the 'jockey' owner still comes only from the neighbouring Ui_JockeyPanel_* run, so the maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_NpcAction_TurnToActor
summary: Starts an NPC action step: takes the target actor id from the action owner (or the object found by Container_FindObjectByTypeId), applies the move speed from Field_NpcAction_GetMoveSpeedById, installs step 0x0032FE7C and feeds a random value when the target has the rotation flag.
evidence: Container_FindObjectByTypeId and Field_NpcAction_GetMoveSpeedById are named, but the speed arrives in in_s0 and the rotation flag/random use is damaged, so the 'turn to actor' semantic is not proven.

name: maybe_Field_NpcAction_IdleB
summary: Twin of 0x0033026C without the target lookup: applies the actor's move speed (from in_s0), installs step 0x0032FE7C, and when the actor animation is ready converts the system speed and applies it through 0x005F5A50.
evidence: The callee set matches 0x0033026C (Field_NpcAction_GetMoveSpeedById, 0x0032FE7C, Os_GetGameWork) but the state word and float conversion use in_s0/in_fpscr, so 'Idle' is only an interpretation of the installed callback; the B suffix merely avoids the name of 0x0039BE90.

name: Battle_ActorAction_Ctor
summary: Tiny constructor of the battle actor-action sub-object: runs Battle_ActionSubObject_BaseCtor and installs the actor-action vtable (g_battleActorActionVtableB).
evidence: The sole caller is the named Battle_ActionAnimWindow_Init, the base is Battle_ActionSubObject_BaseCtor, and the next function 0x0038A59C already carries the name Battle_ActorAction_WaitStart, so this vtable belongs to the actor-action object.

name: Ui_SkillPanel_OnPageInput
signature: void Ui_SkillPanel_OnPageInput(UiSkillPanelWindow* self, void* msg, const UiCommand* cmd, u32 arg4)
summary: Input handler of the skill panel's scrolling page: forwards the pad state to the part at +0x24F8, and on the accept bits clears the UI busy flag and either exits or walks the pane stack looking for the handler's target entry.
evidence: The owner is now pinned by the named Ui_SkillPanelWindow_PopPane and the page part by Ui_Part_ConfirmWithSe1 on self+0x24F8/self+0x170; the body's remaining helpers only decide which entry the page stack selects.

name: Ui_SkillPanel_HandleCommand
summary: Small command handler of the skill panel: commands 0x13/0x14 show or hide the part at +0x1BC, and 0x15 builds a message record (state 2 or 6 from the panel byte +0x2566), applies it to the block at +0x84C and pushes the next pane.
evidence: It dispatches on the command byte and uses the named Ui_SkillPanelWindow_PushPane, Ui_Part_ConfirmWithSe1 and Ui_MessageWindow_SetStatusTextByType, which pins both the owner and the handler role.

name: Ui_Part_CheckAnimConditions
summary: Counts how many of the six animation/entry conditions referenced by table 0x00729EA8 are satisfied for this part and record (member skill ownership through 0x00629988, the part's 60-id list at +0xA0, and the record's status check), returning 1 when at least four pass.
evidence: The named caller Ui_Part_GetAnimState returns this function's result as its states 0/1 and its doc calls that branch the condition check; the callee returns a value in r0 that Ghidra dropped (the header's 'void' is wrong), so the predicate name is genuine and not a Check-on-void trap.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageParts_BuildGlyphParts
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageParts_BuildGlyphParts(UiMessagePartTable* self, int arg2, int* count, int arg4)
summary: Appends the parts for the current page: for each 0x1C-byte page entry whose Ui_Part_GetAnimState returns 3 it fills a 0x18-byte part record with flag bytes 0x10/0x20/1/2/4/8 from entry bytes +0x12..+0x17 and bumps the caller's counter.
evidence: The readable body is still badly damaged (Ghidra lost the frame pointer: register0x00000054, unaff_r4/r5/r7/r10/r11) and the appender 0x003E1848 is unnamed; only the 0x1C stride and the flag constants are verifiable, so this is not item code and the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Effect_SpawnAttachedSingleB
summary: Spawns the single effect of attachment slot at +6: when the cached handle at +0xC8 is stale and the slot id is not -1 it builds the spawn transform through Battle_Effect_ComputeSpawnTransform and creates the instance with Effect_FindOrCreateInstance, caching the new handle.
evidence: The sibling names Effect_SpawnAttachedForSlot / Effect_SpawnAttachedPair and the direct callers place this in that family; the body reads the slot id from the object rather than from a descriptor, so 'FromDescriptor' was wrong, but which attachment slot pair B/C denotes is still unknown.

name: maybe_Effect_SpawnAttachedSingleC
summary: Second single-slot spawner, byte-for-byte twin of 0x00407470: slot id at +0xA, cached handle at +0xD0, spawn transform through Battle_Effect_ComputeSpawnTransform and instance through Effect_FindOrCreateInstance.
evidence: Same named spawn-transform/instance callees as 0x00407470 and the same stale-handle test, with the slot at +0xA; there are no direct callers (it is reached from the target-marker state machine), so the slot semantics stay unproven.

name: Battle_TargetMarker_UpdateSlotEffects
signature: void Battle_TargetMarker_UpdateSlotEffects(EffectAttach* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Per-frame state machine (states 1..4) for the effects attached to a battle target marker: validates the cached effect handles against the 0x7B4D68 table, spawns/updates the slot effects through 0x407468/0x407534 and clears the pending byte +0xE0 when 0x406E08 reports completion.
evidence: Five direct call sites, all inside the now-named Battle_TargetMarker_UpdateSlots, fix the owner; the state-by-state slot handling matches the sibling spawners Effect_SpawnAttachedForSlot/Pair, so the generic 'Effect_UpdateAttachedInstances' name named the wrong object.

name: Ui_FormatMessageArgSpan
summary: Formats the text span of a widget into a message argument slot: selects the span stored at widget+0x208, copies its message line and applies it to argument slot 2 with format 0x006C0025, then returns the requested slot.
evidence: All three callees are named (Ui_SpriteSpan_Select, Text_CopyMessageLine, Message_FormatArgSlot_Reset) and they show the span being copied into the message-arg singleton; that is 'format the message arg from a span', which the old generic wording described correctly.

name: maybe_Party_GetMemberCombatStats
summary: Returns two float combat stats for a party member: reads the member record through 0x0035EB98 and the triple +0x740 / +0xEC0 + +0xB00, with an extra slot lookup and float scaling when the member flag +0xDA bit 7 is set.
evidence: The id goes through func_0035EB98, which FACTS.md identifies as the PartyMember record lookup, so the old 'Monster_GetDefenceStat' named the wrong object; the only caller (Battle_DecideFirstStrike) uses it in its dexterity-based first-strike weighting, but which two stats +0x740 / +0xEC0+0xB00 hold is still not provable.

name: maybe_Battle_GetMemberScaledStat
summary: Looks up the party member behind actor+0x768 and folds the two float tables at member+0xD78 and member+0x1138 for the given stat index, scales by 0.01 and passes the result through the float scaler at 0x00487FC0; returns the battle-work pointer at +0x4238.
evidence: FACTS.md puts this address range in battle combat math, func_0035EB98 makes the actor's +0x768 a party-member index, and 0x00487FC0 is a float scaling/rounding helper (it takes/returns a float in s0), not 'Text_MarkLayoutDirty'; 'Row_CalcActorMetric' therefore described neither a row nor a metric.

name: maybe_Battle_AnimateMemberStatBar
signature: void maybe_Battle_AnimateMemberStatBar(u32 scratch, MonsterWork* work, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, int which)
summary: Updates one displayed member stat: when the guard byte +0x10 is set it looks the party member up by work+0x768, picks +0xB58 or +0xB5C by 'which', compares it with the displayed value at +0xF18 plus the delta, rescales through 0x00487FC0 and calls 0x00496164 to refresh the condition/stat display.
evidence: The three callers are the damage/heal popup spawners (Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnNumberList, SpawnCountBalloon, Battle_QueueActionMessage), the record comes from func_0035EB98 (party member, not monster), and the two float fields +0xB58/+0xB5C are selected by 'which'; the bar/icon identity of 0x00496164 still keeps this at maybe_.

name: Casino_PokerWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the casino poker window: runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs g_casinoPokerWindowVtable (0x77A2B8) and default-constructs its six 0x50-byte score rows with element ctor 0x00326838.
evidence: The body installs the symbol g_casinoPokerWindowVtable and its vtable siblings are already named Casino_PokerWindow_Dtor / Casino_PokerWindow_DtorBase and Ui_PokerScoreList_Init, so the old generic 'Ui_Window_Ctor_vt77A2B8' hid the actual class.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_AttachNamedSpriteA
signature: void maybe_Ui_Panel_AttachNamedSpriteA(UiPanel* self, SpriteActor* panel, int record, u32 flags)
summary: Attaches a named sprite to a panel: clamps the record type byte +9, sets the sprite up with Field_SpriteActor_SetupSpriteA, builds the 0x16-byte pane name from panel+0xAC through 0x0031A73C and creates the frame colour animator.
evidence: The named callees Field_SpriteActor_SetupSpriteA, Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh and Gfx_CreateFColAnimator confirm 'attach sprite A', but the owner is called UiPanel here while the helpers are field sprite-actor functions and there are no callers, so the prefix stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_AttachNamedSpriteB
signature: void maybe_Ui_Panel_AttachNamedSpriteB(UiPanel* self, SpriteActor* panel, int record, u32 flags)
summary: Second named-sprite attach: identical to 0x004DD4A8 but uses Field_SpriteActor_SetupSpriteB before building the 0x16-byte pane name and the colour animator.
evidence: Same body as 0x004DD4A8 with Field_SpriteActor_SetupSpriteB instead of A (same 0x16-byte name build and Gfx_CreateFColAnimator); owner identity and the absence of callers keep the maybe_.

name: maybe_Svc_ContentInfo_IsCacheCurrent
summary: Returns whether the cached content info is at least as new as the system's content version: reads the 0xD0000 system word, fetches the content info under the global monitor and compares the stored halfword at +0x2C with the low half of the system word.
evidence: The named Svc_FetchContentInfo and the monitor lock/unlock are clear, but its callers are only the tentatively named icon-cache loaders and the corrupted Fs_BuildContentInfoArchivePath body, so neither 'Ui_IconCache' nor 'Cecd' is proven; the operation itself is a content-version comparison.

name: maybe_Svc_ContentObject_QuerySize
summary: Queries one content object: reads a 2-byte attribute through vtable+0x2C, allocates a 0x36C0-byte work object (0x0050D708), initialises it, fetches the content info and returns 0 only when the cached size covers the queried value.
evidence: The body creates/initialises a content object (Svc_ContentObject_CreateAndRegister, 0x00503DF0) and fetches content info (Svc_FetchContentInfo), which fixes the content-info subject; nothing in it reads a raw file, so the old 'Cecd_QueryRawFile' wording was speculative.

name: Err_LaunchFatalErrorApplet
summary: Launches the nn::err fatal-error applet for an already filled FatalErrInfo: queries the err service (tolerating the 'already configured' code 0xC8A0CFFC), stops the previous session, runs the err driver setup with the 0xF80 struct and the current display timing, and writes the returned state byte.
evidence: The caller is the named Fs_ReportFatalError, whose body builds the 0xF80-byte nn::err::FatalErrInfo via 0x0051CBF8 and passes it here; FACTS.md records 0x51BA34..0x51CD40 as CTR SDK nn::err (result 0xC8A0CFFC), so the previous 'Sound_Driver_Reconfigure' named the wrong library entirely.

name: Ui_LayoutText_InitStringDescArray
signature: void Ui_LayoutText_InitStringDescArray(unsigned int* self, unsigned int owner, unsigned int value)
summary: Shared initialiser of a layout-text string descriptor: stores the owner at +0 and the value at +0xC, zeroes the header words and constructs the inline two-element (4-byte) array at +0x18.
evidence: Both callers are now the named Ui_LayoutText_InitStringDesc and Ui_LayoutText_InitStringDescSimple, which call this to fill the descriptor; it is the shared body of those two initialisers.

name: maybe_Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureUnitBlock2
signature: unsigned int* maybe_Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureUnitBlock2(void* texState, unsigned int* cmd)
summary: Emits one texture-block GPU command group: packs the state word with bit 0x10000000, writes the command pair 0x000F0093/0x000F0096 and copies the data block from *(texState+8) with the count at *(texState+0xC).
evidence: Both callers are now named draw paths (Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawWithGxState, Gfx_Overlay_DrawSpriteTransition) and the sibling 0x56D544 uses 0x000F0083 with the same layout, but which texture unit/sub-block this '2' variant addresses cannot be decided from the command ids alone.

name: Model_UpdateBlendedAttachmentMatrix
summary: Blends an attachment transform: while the game-work mode pair +0x44/+0x45 is active it resolves the 'N_ALL' anchor once (cached at +0x94), applies the world-wrap offset to both endpoints, computes the anchor via Model_ComputeAttachmentAnchor and slerps both orientation halves back into +4..+0x18 before clearing the pending flag +0x98.
evidence: Every callee is now named (Ui_Overlay_GetAnchorIdByName with the 'N_ALL' literal, Field_ApplyWrapOffsetXZ, Model_ComputeAttachmentAnchor, Math_Vec3Slerp) and the body writes the two transform halves in place, so 'blended attachment matrix' is literal rather than inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowRefText
summary: Posts the text row referenced by a message-window entry: picks the row id from the current record (or its +0xD2 reference), spawns the popup entry through Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForRefList and, when the row is visible and plain, pushes a second message through Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry.
evidence: It is a vtable slot 0x28 body of the message-window family and uses named Text_IsRowVisible / Text_Style_IsPlainRecord / Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForRefList, so the old 'Battle_Ui_ShowMemberRefText' over-specified an unproven member/battle owner; no caller pins the window class.

name: Field_Object_Kind08_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the field object for script object-factory kind 8: runs the field-party base constructor, installs vtable 0x0077E10C, sets the +0x3784 block to -1/0, constructs the child at -0xDE18 and clears its +0xDC and +0xDE0F bytes.
evidence: The caller is the named Field_ObjectFactory_Kind08, the base is FieldParty_Ctor, and the vtable/offset pattern matches the other field-object kind constructors; the factory kind is the only identity available and the name states exactly that.

name: Ui_TextScreen_Ctor_77E6B8
summary: Constructor of a text-cache screen: Ui_Screen_CtorWithTextCache, vtable 0x77E6B8, the -1/0 defaults at +0xC98/+0xC99, resets the member slot and clears the extra words at +0xC9D, +0x3279 and +0xC9E.
evidence: The caller is the named Field_ObjectFactory_Kind01 and the base Ui_Screen_CtorWithTextCache is shared with the 0x0059DE54 sibling; the screen's purpose is still only the vtable, so 0.5 rather than higher.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowAndStoreArgs
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowAndStoreArgs(void* self, void* ctx, int* args)
summary: Places one gimmick list row at the owner actor's position offset by args[0] (scaled), re-applies the row asset id from args[6], copies the 0x11-byte argument block into the state record at +0x1A8..+0x1C0 and signals the state machine through the handle ref.
evidence: Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId and std_memcpy are named and the +0x1A8 argument block is explicit, but the placement helper 0x005D2A00 is still unnamed and the function has no direct callers, so 'PlaceRow' remains an inference.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetFromArgs
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetFromArgs(void* self, int arg2, int* args)
summary: Three-statement wrapper: resolves the gimmick owner through f_154C, converts args[1] to float (the result is discarded in the readable C) and forwards *args to Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId for row 0.
evidence: The only body is the named Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId call; the float conversion and the 0x004A1E00 owner lookup return values were dropped by Ghidra, so the 'from args' summary is only accurate for the asset id.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowsAndStoreArgs
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowsAndStoreArgs(void* self, void* arg2, int* args)
summary: Places two gimmick rows at the owner actor's current position (asset id args[5] at index 1 and args[2] at index -1), stores the actor/handle pair at +0x2DC/+0x2E0 and signals the handle-linked state machine.
evidence: Two named Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId calls with the position from 0x004A1E00 support 'place rows', but there are no callers and the +0x2D4 value passed to 0x005E5140 is still unexplained.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_GetCursorRowState
summary: Hit-tests the list under the cursor (id list at +0x288, mask 0x40) and dispatches on the picked component's class: bag rows return Ui_BagList_GetRowState, equipment rows return a weapon-type code through Ui_Equipment_GetWeaponType(A).
evidence: The callees are now named and the caller maybe_Menu_ApplyRowColorState maps the result to colour commands, but the equipment branch returns a weapon type while the bag branch returns a row state, so the result is a mixed 'row kind/state' and the display-column reading is still open.

name: maybe_Item_CheckCraftRequirements
signature: u32 maybe_Item_CheckCraftRequirements(u32 arg1, RecipeWork* recipe, u32 scratch, u32 scratch2)
summary: Checks the six 10-byte requirement rows of a recipe: skips the check when the work bytes +0x2D549/+0x2D54A are clear, then for each non-empty row compares the item id and quantity range and stops at the first row whose extra status check fails.
evidence: The row layout (u16 id, min/max, three option bytes) and the terminal maybe_Field_Object_IsStatusFull call are clear, but this address range's callers still carry unreliable camera-style names, so 'craft recipe' (smith) remains a strong but unproven reading.

name: Ui_SmithMenu_GetMaterialCellRecordKey
summary: Resolves the smith-menu material cell under the cursor (index into the widget's u16 cell table at +0x50) and returns the first u16 of the record that the Game_GetDataManager lookup yields.
evidence: Its three callers are the named Ui_SmithMenu_HandleMaterialList / ExecuteCommand / ExecuteCommand_Part2, which feed the result to Ui_Row_SetIndex; the body is the twin of the named Ui_SmithMenu_GetMaterialCellValue.

name: Ui_SmithMenu_ResolveMaterialCellRecord
summary: Material-cell accessor: computes the same cell index as Ui_SmithMenu_GetMaterialCellValue, resolves that cell id's record through 0x0063E998 and returns the record pointer used to fill the material rows.
evidence: In Ui_SmithMenu_HandleMaterialList and Ui_SmithMenu_ExecuteCommand the return value is passed directly as the row-record argument to Ui_SmithMenu_FillMaterialRows immediately after the cursor query, which fixes both the data flow and the 'resolve record' wording.

name: maybe_Ui_ScrollList_MoveCursorWithPage
signature: void maybe_Ui_ScrollList_MoveCursorWithPage(void* self, int delta, u32 arg3, int pageCount)
summary: Page-aware cursor mover for a scrolling list: adds the delta to the row index, clamps it with the item count and, when the last page is only partly filled, recomputes the page start/size and re-selects the entry before refreshing the rows.
evidence: The visible half matches the sibling 0x006E51E4 and ends in Ui_List_SelectEntryById, but the body is truncated by 'bad instruction data' (halt_baddata) and uses unaff_r6, so the page-clamping branch cannot be verified.

name: Gfx_InitDefaultTexture
summary: Creates the engine's 16x16 default texture: stores the renderer handle from cfg+4, opens the graphics/OS session, allocates 16x16x1 storage through the renderer callback, registers it with Fs_MountByName and marks the slot valid.
evidence: The only caller is the named Engine_Initialize and it pairs explicitly with Gfx_ReleaseDefaultTexture (0x00104F58), which unmounts and frees the same slot; the fixed 16x16x1 allocation identifies the texture, though no string names its purpose.

name: Gfx_ReleaseDefaultTexture
summary: Releases the default texture created by 0x00104ED8: unmounts it with Fs_UnmountByName, runs the renderer object's virtual destructor on the handle at +0x10, frees the OS resource and clears the valid flag, handle and owner pointer.
evidence: The named Engine_Initialize/Engine_ShutdownAllSubsystems call it on the same global slot initialised by 0x00104ED8 and the mount/unmount calls mirror each other exactly.

name: maybe_Mem_QueryMemoryMode
summary: Lock-protected service query (request 0x0301/0x11) whose reply is normalised to 1 or 2 and stored as the allocator's memory-mode word.
evidence: The only caller is the named Mem_InitAllocatorState, which stores the result in allocator state +8 immediately after the extended-memory probes; the body has no sound code at all, so the old 'Snd_QueryDspState' prefix was wrong, but the exact service/mode meaning is still unidentified.

name: maybe_Snd_ShutdownEngine
signature: void maybe_Snd_ShutdownEngine(void* engine, u32 arg2, u32* mask, int count)
summary: Stops the sound engine: marks f_358/f_348, waits on and closes the session handle at f_344, releases the command buffer at f_340, then walks a caller-supplied bitmask and releases each set 0x1C-byte voice record at f_24 + i*0x1C.
evidence: The callees (0x0010DF40/0x0010DF90, Snd_ReleaseAllChannels) and the voice-record bitmask fit 'release these voices', but Ghidra lost unaff_r5/r6/r8/r11 and the Thumb body has overlapping instructions, so whole-engine shutdown vs per-call release is still open.

name: maybe_Snd_StreamManager_ServiceSlots
signature: void maybe_Snd_StreamManager_ServiceSlots(void* self, u32 arg2, int count)
summary: Services the stream manager's pending slot batch under the shared mutex: walks the bitmask at self+0x2C, and for every set bit with a live 0x1C-byte entry at self+0x24 completes its stream/object, releases the channel and bumps the completed counter at +0x70.
evidence: Its only real caller is the named Snd_StreamManager_Update, and the body loops over the same 0x1C-byte voice/stream records as Snd_ShutdownEngine, calling Snd_ReleaseAllChannels/Snd_Channel_Release and Fs_SubmitAsyncTransfer; there is no texture-upload code, so 'Gfx_UploadQueuedTextures' named the wrong subsystem.

name: maybe_Gfx_StartGpuWorkerThread
signature: void maybe_Gfx_StartGpuWorkerThread(u32 namePtr, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Starts the shared GPU/service worker: creates three kernel objects in globals 0x7EDFA4.., substitutes the two handles supplied by the caller, initialises the 0x7AF0B4 event and starts thread 0x00113F2C with a small argument block.
evidence: The caller is the named Mem_MapSharedBlock (which maps the GPU shared block and passes the two returned words), and the thread proc 0x00113F2C is used by the display-transfer path 0x0010CF50 and Sound_Driver_Shutdown; no service is opened, so 'Os_OpenServiceHandle' was wrong.

name: maybe_Snd_ProcessPendingStreams
summary: Handles pending stream stops: when the queue object at 0x007AEA98 has bits set that are not yet acknowledged it signals the completion event at +8, marks the busy flags and drives the stream context through 0x001132DC.
evidence: It operates on the same 0x7AEA98 queue object and 0x7EF414 context as the frame prologue 0x0010C90C, but the callee 0x001132DC is a stream-context teardown, which contradicts 'ResumeChannels'; the caller side is still missing, so a vague 'process pending streams' is the honest reading.

name: maybe_Gfx_ServiceDisplayTransfer
signature: int maybe_Gfx_ServiceDisplayTransfer(u32* outA, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int* outB, u32* outC, u32 arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8)
summary: Display-transfer state machine: repeatedly submits Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer, waits out the transient GSP status codes (1, 0xA-0x12, 0x40/0x41), maps the final code to an engine display state and drives the enable/disable transitions through Gfx_IpcCmd50100.
evidence: The callers are now named Gfx_UpdateDisplayState/Gfx_UpdateDisplayStateB/Gfx_WaitForIpcIdle and the body loops on Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer with the GSP status set, so this services a transfer rather than 'negotiating' a display mode; the exact meaning of the returned state codes is still open.

name: Os_QueuePopUntilId
summary: Blocks on the queue embedded at owner+0xB4 and pops entries until the one whose id field equals the requested id arrives, refreshing the owner's current-entry fields +0x178/+0x184/+0x188/+0x18C and clearing them when the last entry is popped.
evidence: The callee is the named Os_QueuePopBlocking and the seven callers span sound (Snd_QueueWaveCommand, Sound_StreamPlayer_Shutdown), archive (0x00543484) and the container/RB-tree helpers, so this is a generic queue primitive; the old 'Snd_' prefix named only one user.

name: Save_BuildSectionList
summary: Builds the save-snapshot block list: walks the 0x274C-byte handler table at self+0x34, invokes each handler, chains the returned blocks into a list with a running id and pushes the head through Os_QueueTryPush.
evidence: The callers are the named SaveData_ResetAllSaveData and Item_ValidateAndCompactStorage, and the table dispatch plus the tagged list chained at self+0x16C..+0x174 matches save-snapshot construction; the handler block format is still unknown.
